articles.title: JAPEX Eyes More Than 10,000 Boe/d in Norway with Goliat Deal
articles.description: Japan Petroleum Exploration (JAPEX) has agreed to buy an 8% stake in Norway’s Goliat oil field from Equinor as it aims to exceed 10,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day in the country in the 2030s. Under two linked agreements announced Wednesday, JAPEX will pay Equinor $65 million in cash and transfer its 3.5% stake in the Verdande field. In return, it will acquire the Goliat stake, interests in nearby discoveries and exploration acreage in the Norwegian Sea. articles.description: Saipem has secured two offshore contracts worth around $650m from Aramco for EPCI work at five fields in Saudi Arabia.

articles.title: Kazakhstan Joins Iraq in Pushing OPEC+ for a Higher Capacity Rating
articles.description: Kazakhstan has joined Iraq in asking OPEC+ to raise its estimate of the country's crude production capacity, Reuters reported Wednesday, citing people familiar with the matter. The request comes four days before the group meets to set its output policy for 2027. The review is OPEC's first, and will assess how much oil each member can produce sustainably, and its findings will help set production targets for next year. articles.title: U.S. Diplomatic Push Revives Hopes for Trans-Caspian Gas Pipeline
articles.description: Trans-Caspian connectivity was the topic du jour during US Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau’s November 23 talks with Turkmen leaders in Ashgabat. Readouts of Landau’s meetings hinted that a trans-Caspian pipeline was among the central items on the agenda. articles.title: Aramco Opens $7 Billion Petrochemical Complex in South Korea
articles.description: Saudi Aramco on Wednesday officially launched a $7-billion petrochemicals complex in South Korea as the oil giant expands its downstream presence in its key crude export market, Asia. Saudi Aramco and its South Korean subsidiary S-OIL inaugurated the Shaheen Project in Seoul, which took $7 billion in investment, Aramco’s single biggest investment in the Asian country. articles.title: Expro wins three-year flow management deal in Alaska

articles.title: Oil Inventories Continue to Rise in the US
articles.description: Crude oil inventories in the United States saw an increase of 1.1 million barrels during the week ending November 20, according to new data from the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) released on Wednesday. The increase brings commercial stockpiles to 418.9 million barrels, according to government data, which is now 3% below the five-year average for this time of year. The EIA’s data release follows API’s figures that were released a day earlier, which reported that crude oil inventories had risen by 126,000 barrels in the…

articles.title: Oil Jumps Over 2% as Saudi Arabia Downs Drones Over Ras Tanura
articles.description: Oil prices climbed on Wednesday after Yemen's Houthis claimed a strike on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery, the kingdom's largest, and Saudi Arabia said it had shot down four drones over the site. As of 10:16 a.m. ET, Brent crude traded at $93.60 per barrel, up $2.20 or 2.41%, and West Texas Intermediate traded at $83.51, up $1.46 or 1.78%. Saudi-led coalition spokesman Turki Al-Maliki said air defenses destroyed four drones over Ras Tanura on Wednesday morning, and that fragments fell from the interceptions with no injuries in an initial assessment.…

articles.title: UK Energy Bills Set to Soar 26% as Iran War Drives Up Gas Prices
articles.description: Energy bills for households across Britain are set to rocket from the start of next year, in a further blow to households struggling with the cost of living. Bills will surge by 26 per cent from 1 January, energy regulator Ofgem has confirmed. Ofgem said the energy price cap will rise from £1,723 to £2,166 for typical annual energy bills. The increase, which leaves the cap at its highest level in more than three years, comes on top of already high energy costs. The price cap increased by 4 per cent at the start of last month. It’s…

articles.title: Iran War Is Pushing Record Numbers of Fuel Tankers Into Crude Trade
articles.description: The Middle East crisis and upended crude and fuel flows have accelerated a shift in the global tanker fleet that began last year. A growing number of the so-called long-range-2 (LR2) clean tankers that have transported fuels such as diesel and gasoline have become the so-called dirty tankers and started shipping crude. As of this week, a record-high share of 75% of the global LR2 fleet is engaged in dirty crude transportation, while the number and share of tankers moving petroleum products, the so-called clean vessels, have dropped to record lows,…

articles.title: UK Energy Price Cap Jumps 26% in January, Highest Since 2023
articles.description: Energy prices for UK households will surge by 26% from January 1 as the Middle East war is pushing wholesale gas prices higher, the UK’s energy regulator Ofgem said in its quarterly energy cap announcement on Wednesday. The UK has a so-called Energy Price Cap in place, which protects households from excessively high bills by capping the price that energy utility providers can pass on to them.
